chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran or someone else, from Aasim ibn Humyd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'A man bequeathed to a man a bequest from his wealth, a third or a quarter. The man was killed in error, meaning the testator.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'This bequest is held from his inheritance and from his blood money (diyah).'
ai.seo_question: Does a bequest get paid from the blood money of the deceased?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that in cases of qatl al-khata' (killing by error), the testator's bequest is satisfied from both his general estate and the blood money (diyah) received, treating the latter as part of the inheritable wealth. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view that diyah is a financial asset subject to the deceased's final wishes, distinct from the specific distribution rules of the Quranic shares. It underscores the principle that the testator retains disposal rights over all acquired assets, including compensation for his life, until the bequest is fulfilled.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Najran or someone else, from Aasim Bin Humyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>,

‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man bequeathed to a man with a bequest with regards to his wealth, a third or a quarter. The man was killed in error, meaning the testator’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Hold on for this bequest from his inheritance and from his wergild (blood money compensation)’.
en.sarwar: 21. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Najran and others from “Asem ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Qays who has narrated the following: “I once said to abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

that a man made a will to another man about his assets, one-third or one-fourth of his legacy, and then the testator is killed mistakenly. He (the Imam) said, ‘Funds must be kept aside for this will from his legacy and the wergild.’”
